name: Ovalbumin
biological_source: Egg white (Gallus gallus albumen, 54% of total protein)
solubility: Freely soluble in neutral and mildly alkaline water
chemical_rationale: High proportion of hydrophobic residues in the interior that unfold irreversibly upon shear stress at the air-water interface, presenting hydrophobic side chains toward the gas phase and hydrophilic residues toward the lamellar water, producing an elastic 2D viscoelastic network.

name: Ovotransferrin (Conalbumin)
biological_source: Egg white (Gallus gallus albumen, 12% of total protein)
chemical_rationale: Lowest thermal denaturation threshold among major egg albumen proteins (61°C); binds Fe3+ and Cu2+; rapidly forms disulfide-mediated aggregates that seed early custard and meringue setting.

name: Ovomucin Complex
biological_source: Thick egg white albumen (3.5% of total protein)
solubility: Insoluble in pure water; dispersible in salt solution at neutral/alkaline pH
chemical_rationale: Forms massive fibrous networks with lysozyme that entrap fluid lamellae between bubbles, conferring extreme shear resistance and preventing rapid bubble drainage.

name: Casein Micellar Complex
formula: Colloidal phosphoprotein assembly (alpha-s1, alpha-s2, beta, kappa caseins)
structure_type: Spherical colloidal aggregate (50-300 nm) stabilized by colloidal calcium phosphate
biological_source: Bovine milk (80% of total milk protein)
solubility: Colloidal suspension; stable to 140°C boiling at pH 6.7
chemical_rationale: Kappa-casein C-terminal hydrophilic glycopeptide hairs protrude outward providing strong steric and electrostatic repulsion; collapses upon acidification to pH 4.6 or enzymatic chymosin cleavage, precipitating into curd.

name: Beta-Lactoglobulin
structure_type: Globular lipocalin protein with calyx binding pocket
biological_source: Bovine whey (50% of total whey protein)
chemical_rationale: Contains a single buried free sulfhydryl group (Cys121). Upon heating past 78°C, the tertiary structure unfolds, exposing Cys121 to participate in thiol-disulfide exchange with other whey proteins or kappa-casein.

name: Whey Protein Isolate Complex
biological_source: Cheese whey effluent, ultrafiltered and microfiltered
chemical_rationale: High surface activity enables rapid adsorption at newly created interfaces, generating fine bubble dispersions with rapid film cross-linking upon heat curing.

name: Triacylglycerols (Triglycerides)
structure_type: Glycerol esterified with three fatty acid chains
biological_source: Milkfat and egg yolk lipid core
chemical_rationale: When liquid/free, triglycerides spread competitively at air-water interfaces, displacing elastic protein films and collapsing egg white foams. When partially crystallized in refrigerated cream (4-8°C), solid fat needles pierce droplet membranes during shear, creating a coherent 3D fat-crystal continuous network that traps air bubbles.

name: Phospholipids (Phosphatidylcholine / Lecithin)
structure_type: Amphiphilic glycerol backbone with two fatty acids and polar choline phosphodiester
biological_source: Egg yolk (28% of yolk lipid) and soybean oil
solubility: Dispersible in water forming lamellar bilayer and liposomal phases
chemical_rationale: Zwitterionic headgroup and hydrophobic tail grant intense surface activity, lowering oil-water interfacial tension to < 2 mN/m; competitively displaces slower proteins from droplet surfaces through Oris-Gibbs Marangoni effects.

name: Sucrose
chemical_rationale: Forms eight hydrogen bonds with surrounding water molecules per molecule, raising aqueous phase viscosity exponentially and immobilizing bulk water, dramatically retarding capillary drainage from foam bubble lamellae.

name: Xanthan Polysaccharide
structure_type: Cellulosic beta-(1,4)-D-glucan backbone with trisaccharide side chains
chemical_rationale: Rigid 5-fold helical conformation in solution forms a dynamic 3D physical network with significant yield stress at low shear rates, halting liquid drainage between foam bubbles completely.

name: Potassium Bitartrate
chemical_rationale: Partially dissociates in water releasing H+ ions to lower pH to 4.8-5.0, directly adjacent to the isoelectric point of ovalbumin (pI 4.5), diminishing negative carboxylate charge repulsion.
